method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file: title and title.canDo, the Folge (7 lines and the gist item), the 3 inputs (30 lines), the flyer (49 words), 10 exam texts, 2 strategy cards, 8 redemittel, both speaking parts (instructionsDe, situationDe, cards, openingLine, hintWords, 16 model turns), the writing task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte, checklist, model text), 4 check lines, the story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, every promptDe, option and explanation.de, and the two new facts[] records. We solved all 95 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: 1 start gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 33 pool items, 12 reserve, 10 exam items, 8 check items and 4 proof items. For sentence_building we permuted the tiles and checked every V2 and V1 order against accepted[]. For error_correction we tried every one-word correction, including deletions. We traced the generators (3 × dictation.fromInput on 6 sources without `say`, 3 × numbers.dictation, 2 × lex.articlePlural, 1 × lex.glossTyped, 3 × lex.glossMatch) against the lexicon roles. We ran 18 candidate learner answers through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (for example „Wir brauchen Brot.“ on ls1-p10, „die“ on c01, „10“ on q04, „neun“ on ls2-i05). We confirmed that the player now shuffles non-exam options: src/lib/course-v2/unitPlan.js orderedOptions is called from ItemView.jsx l. 96, with a seed of unit, item and attempt. We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: h1 is 6 × abc with 3 options, 2 plays, [32–53] words and the textVariantDe scaffold; h2 is 4 × R/F with 1 play and [29–47] words; sp2 has two topics with cards-ask; sp3 uses cards-request; s2 has 3 Leitpunkte and about 30 words. Every exam text is original in the official format. We recounted with the validator's wordCount: h1 50/41/37/41/37/38, h2 31/31/32/30, model text 26 and cliffhanger 25. We ran the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u04 over every German surface (not only inputs: prompts, options, explanations, instructions, checklist, title.canDo, endLines) and looked up each unknown token's allocation in all eight lexicons. We read story and cast against the authored a1.1 units now on disk (u01, u02, u03, u05, u07; u03 and u05 are new since r4), against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (ensemble genders: -1/-2 f, -3/-4 m, which match every stem and explanation), and against curriculum/a1-1.json u04. We recomputed every sum. The market comes to 2,20 + 3,60 + 0,90 + 1,80 + 0,50 = 9,00 ✓. The whole Saturday comes to 9,24 + 9,00 + 5,37 = 23,61 € plus 2,00 € Pfand (six water and two milk bottles at 0,25 €) out of the 50 € ✓. The agent proxy let gesetze-im-internet.de and revosax.sachsen.de through in this session, so both facts were re-read at the source (see r4-F05). Every r1–r4 finding was verified against the current file and the current rails.

findings.problem: The German prompt only says „Korrigieren Sie:“. Deleting the wrong article is an equally correct correction. „Wir brauchen Brot.“ is standard German (Brot as a mass noun), and it is the exact frame the unit models in the Folge (l02) and dictates in its own scored Check (c06). The v2 grader, run on the item, marks it wrong and shows „Wir brauchen ein Brot.“. So a learner who writes correct German, in the sentence shape the unit taught, is told it is false. §9.4 lists „a defensible second answer not accepted“ as MAJOR. The unit's other article corrections are safe only by accident. c07's one-word deletion is ungrammatical („Ich brauche Kilo Äpfel“). ls3-p10 admits „Ich möchte die Tomaten.“ only through a two-word deletion. ls3-r04 carries no errorTag at all. The class is not new. b2.2-u04 r1 F14 and r2 F04, and a2.2-u04 r1 F05 (all MAJOR), found bare „Korrigieren Sie:“ items that reject a correct alternative correction. The rule b2.2-u04 r2 F04 proposed (the German prompt names what to correct) was never written. ITM-01 still checks only that the quoted sentence and intentionalError exist. So the gate let the class into a unit that four rounds had passed, and §9.4 also rates a gate hole that lets a finding class through as MAJOR.
findings.fix: Unit, 4 promptDe edits, all ≤ 90 characters; the keys do not change: ls1-p10 „Korrigieren Sie den Artikel: „Wir brauchen eine Brot.““ (54), c07 „Korrigieren Sie den Artikel: „Ich brauche eine Kilo Äpfel.““ (59), ls3-p10 „Korrigieren Sie den Artikel: „Ich möchte ein Kilo die Tomaten.““ (63) and ls3-r04 „Korrigieren Sie den Artikel: „Wir brauchen 500 Gramm der Käse.““ (63). „Artikel“ is metalanguage the unit already uses („(bestimmter Artikel)“, „Welcher Artikel passt?“). The prompt then rules out both the article deletion in ls1-p10 and the quantity deletion in ls3-p10. Do not only widen accepted[] (CLAUDE.md: the rule belongs in the checker or the build, with a test). If the author prefers to accept „Wir brauchen Brot.“, it needs acceptedWhy „grammatisch: Brot ohne Artikel, wie in „Wir brauchen Brot und Käse.““ and the rail below. Rule-smith: write the rail. This is the §9.4 5th-round remedy, and it replaces a 6th content round.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01: an error_correction item whose planted error is an article or a word-order error (errorTag or errorTags[0] in gender-article, case, v2-inv, verb-final, connector-position or satzklammer, or no errorTag at all) names the corrected category in promptDe („den Artikel“, „die Endung“, „die Wortstellung“, „die Verbform“ …), unless every alternative correction is in accepted[] with acceptedWhy. Failing fixture: a1.1-u04 ls1-p10 with the bare „Korrigieren Sie:“; passing: „Korrigieren Sie den Artikel: …“. The test runs over all registered courses (b2.2-u04 r2 F04, a2.2-u04 r1 F05 and this finding are the same class).

findings.problem: This is the 4th round with both cards unchanged (r2-F09, r3-F06, r4-F07). The indefinite rule and its unlabelled table row are true only in the nominative, but every frame of the unit is accusative (brauchen, möchte, kaufen).
